title: Japan food consumption-tax cut takes effect (8% to 1% for two years) — mechanical CPI drag
source: NEWS: two independent syndications read in full 2026-09-05. News On Japan, 'BOJ Rate Pressure Puts Takaichi's Economic Agenda Under Scrutiny', dated 2026-08-07 (newsonjapan.com/article/150291.php, HTTP 200, 31,418 bytes, fetched direct): 'The ruling Liberal Democratic Party has approved Takaichi's plan to reduce the consumption tax on food from 8% to 1% for two years from April 2027, pending parliamentary approval. The government also plans payments that would effectively cover the remaining 1%, making food tax-free for households during the period.' Corroborated by vatcalc.com and Japan Today ('Japan to cut consumption tax on food to 1% from April 2027: PM'), which add that the measure is 'to be replaced in 2029 by a new refundable tax credit system'. PENDING DIET PASSAGE as of the 2026-08-07 source date — this is an announced-and-party-approved policy, not law, which is precisely what `estimate` is for. The autumn Diet session is the venue that settles it
notes: DISCOVERED during the boj-decision-2027-01-22 initial-research adjacency sweep (2026-09-05). It is on this calendar for one reason: it is a large, dated, MECHANICAL drag on Japanese CPI landing on the first day of FY2027, and the Bank of Japan must publish an FY2027 CPI projection that either books it or strips it — a decision first visible at boj-decision-2027-01-22 (Outlook Report) and first testable against realised data at boj-decision-2027-04-28. ARITHMETIC, STATED AS THIS LANE'S OWN ESTIMATE AND NOT A SOURCED NUMBER: cutting the reduced rate from 8% to 1% lowers affected retail prices by about 7/108, roughly 6.5%; Japan's reduced rate applies to food and non-alcoholic beverages excluding dining out, plus newspapers, so the affected share of the CPI basket is materially narrower than the ~26% 'food' aggregate. Against a plausible 16-22% affected weight that is a one-off drag of roughly 1.0-1.4 percentage points on year-on-year CPI for the twelve months from April 2027, unwinding in April 2029. The precise weight is NOT sourced here — the Statistics Bureau item-weight tables were not extracted — so treat the magnitude as an order-of-magnitude bound, not a figure. The government's plan to make separate payments covering the residual 1% does NOT show up in CPI at all (a transfer, not a price), so it widens the household-income effect without changing the index arithmetic. Fiscal side, press-cited: revenue shortfall put at about 4.4-5 trillion yen a year (roughly 10 trillion over the two years) with the administration promising no deficit-financing bonds — the funding credibility question that has been pushing JGB long yields, which is the one channel by which this could reach a US equity book at all, and it is second-order and already owned by the FOMC ledgers. Impact is LOW: symbols is empty and no house playbook is keyed to Japanese fiscal policy.
